reconstruction:
D01: For each fixed target exhaustion T and guessed set B, the supremum over all exhaustions Q with Q.limit = B of liminf_n membershipFraction(Q_n,T_n) equals liminf_n membershipFraction(B,T_n). In the left expression the numerator counts target-stage elements already in the simultaneous guessed stage; the right counts target-stage elements in the entire guessed set. The outer result is equality of real numbers, with no maximizer or procedure named.

D02: For every f, set L, and fixed infinite-limit guessed exhaustion Q satisfying |ΔQ_(n+1)| ≤ f(n+1) for every n, the supremum over target exhaustions T of L that satisfy the same bound f of liminf_n membershipFraction(T_n,Q_n) equals liminf_n membershipFraction(L,Q_n). Both the target and guessed bounds use positive step indices. This is a supremum equality for the fixed Q, not an existential learner theorem.

D03: The value is the atTop liminf of the fraction of distinct cumulative guessed-stage elements belonging to L. For a nonempty Q_n it is |{x ∈ Q_n : x ∈ L}| / |Q_n|; for an empty stage the fraction is defined to be zero.

D04: Relative to a fixed injective enumeration e of K.carrier, this is the liminf of the fraction of the first n enumerated target positions whose values lie in B. The n = 0 prefix ratio is zero; for n > 0 it is |{i < n : e(i) ∈ B}| / n.
quantifiers_and_dependencies:
D01: ∀ target : Exhaustion, ∀ guess : Language, bestExhaustionLowerRecall target guess = coverageLowerRecall target guess.

D02: ∀ f : Nat → Nat, ∀ L : Language, ∀ Q : Exhaustion, Infinite(Q.limit) → BoundedBy f Q → bestBoundedLowerPrecision f L Q = lowerMembershipPrecision L Q.

D03: lowerMembershipPrecision : Language → Exhaustion → Real; lowerMembershipPrecision L Q := liminf_(n→∞) membershipFraction L Q_n.

D04: lowerRecall : OrderedLanguage → Language → Real; lowerRecall K B := K.lowerDensity B = liminf_(n→∞) K.prefixRatio B n.
algorithm_scope:
D01: No learner is quantified. T is a whole mathematical exhaustion and B an arbitrary set. The supremum ranges over semantic exhaustions of that same B, without a bound or effectiveness requirement.

D02: The alternatives T in the supremum may depend on f, L, and the fixed entire Q. Their existence/effectiveness and an attaining witness are not separately asserted by this type. Sets are predicates with classical finite filtering.

D03: This is a statistic of the whole exhaustion and set, with no learner or computation interface. Membership filtering uses classical proposition decidability.

D04: The target contains its full mathematical enumeration, injectivity, and range-equals-carrier evidence. No representation or effective access to that enumeration or to membership in B is specified.
limitations:
D01: No infinitude assumption on T or B. Empty T_n contributes zero under the cumulative fraction convention; an empty or eventually exhausted target is allowed. This is a liminf identity, not an all-time, attained-maximum, or rate statement.

D02: The guessed limit must be infinite. f need not be monotone or everywhere positive; f(0) is unused. With f identically zero there is no admissible infinite Q, so the implication is vacuous. No ordered target, novelty, tail precision, convergence rate, or oracle program is asserted.

D03: It measures cumulative-stage membership precision, not the newest increment and not a probability law. Empty exhaustion has value zero. Repeated proposals do not multiply counts because stages are finite sets; no convergence beyond a liminf is built into the definition.

D04: The enumeration cannot repeat values and forces an infinite target carrier. B may be empty or arbitrary and need not be a subset of the carrier. Recall depends on the supplied order, concerns the entire set B, and is a deterministic lower density rather than time-indexed prediction accuracy or a probability.

reconstruction:
D05: Every exhaustion with at most c new distinct elements in each positive step has a time N at which its step tail precision equals its lower tail precision, and every subsequent step tail precision is at least that same lower value. The witness N can depend on L, Q, c, and the bound evidence.

D06: If every positive increment has at most one element, then the lower tail precision is either zero or one, and there is N with stepTailPrecision(N) equal to that lower value and all later step values at least it. These are two conjuncts; the attainment conjunct has both equality-at-N and the all-later lower bound.

D07: For every L and exhaustion Q, eventual validity of every newly added element is equivalent to step tail precision being exactly one at every sufficiently late step. The existential cutoffs on the two sides are separate witnesses inside the equivalence.
quantifiers_and_dependencies:
D05: ∀ {L : Language} {Q : Exhaustion} {c : Nat}, BoundedBy (fun _ => c) Q → ∃ N, stepTailPrecision L Q N = lowerTailPrecision L Q ∧ ∀ n ≥ N, lowerTailPrecision L Q ≤ stepTailPrecision L Q n.

D06: ∀ {L : Language} {Q : Exhaustion}, IsSingleStep Q → (lowerTailPrecision L Q = 0 ∨ lowerTailPrecision L Q = 1) ∧ LowerTailPrecisionAttained L Q.

D07: ∀ L : Language, ∀ Q : Exhaustion, (∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ΔQ_n ⊆ L) ↔ (∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, stepTailPrecision L Q n = 1).
algorithm_scope:
D05: No generator or algorithm to find N is supplied. The conclusion is semantic finite-time attainment plus a permanent lower bound.

D06: No learner or computable decision between the disjuncts, and no method for finding N, is quantified.

D07: No learner, rate, or procedure for obtaining a cutoff is given. This is an equivalence of predicates of the fixed trace.
limitations:
D05: c may be zero; then all increments are empty and their step precision is one. No infinite limit or nonempty-step assumption is imposed. Attainment does not say the sequence is eventually constant or converges, and no bound on N is provided.

D06: Single-step means at most one new element, allowing empty increments, finite limits, and an empty exhaustion. Empty increments score one. In the zero branch the result does not force eventual constancy; in the one branch the all-later bound yields step values one. The claim is about liminf of increments, not cumulative membership precision.

D07: Empty increments are valid subsets and have step precision one; finite or empty traces are included. The right side is eventual exact equality of the step statistic, not merely lowerTailPrecision = 1. Earlier invalid elements may remain in cumulative stages.

reconstruction: D08: For a single fixed ordered target K, fixed output set, and real α, if its same lower density is at least α/(2 + 4/s) for every natural s ≥ 2, then it is at least α/2. The output is fixed before the universal s; no changing family of output sets is being compared.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D08: ∀ K : OrderedLanguage, ∀ output : Language, ∀ α : Real, (∀ s : Nat, 2 ≤ s → α / (2 + 4 / (s : Real)) ≤ K.lowerDensity output) → α / 2 ≤ K.lowerDensity output.
algorithm_scope: D08: No generator, construction of output, or effective access is provided. All approximating bounds are hypotheses, not conclusions of an algorithm analysis in this type.
limitations:
D08: There is no sign or interval restriction on α and no assertion that any output satisfying the premise exists. The scale parameter s is natural and at least two, not a sample-time-dependent choice. No rate is asserted.

reconstruction: D09: For each ordered target, validity set L, and step bound f, there is one generator G that works for every subsequently chosen exhaustion A with infinite limit, limit contained in L, and positive increments bounded by f. For its specifically generated Q, all three conclusions hold: the same increment bound f, lower target recall exactly one, and cumulative lower membership precision in L exactly one.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D09: ∀ target : OrderedLanguage, ∀ L : Language, ∀ f : Nat → Nat, ∃ G : BatchGenerator, ∀ A : Exhaustion, Infinite(A.limit) → A.limit ⊆ L → BoundedBy f A → let Q := generatedExhaustion G A; BoundedBy f Q ∧ lowerRecall target Q.limit = 1 ∧ lowerMembershipPrecision L Q = 1.
algorithm_scope: D09: G is selected after target, L, and f and before A, so the existential can depend on all three fixed parameters but must be uniform over admissible A. Its online arguments are exactly those in G05: current index, cumulative adversary history through the current stage, and previous cumulative guess. The existential names no witness and supplies no computability or restricted membership-oracle contract; parameters may be captured in the chosen mathematical function.
limitations:
D09: No target.carrier ⊆ L assumption, novelty conclusion, tail-precision conclusion, exact all-time precision, or rate appears. If L is finite, or if f permits no infinite bounded A (for example f identically zero), the universal implication is vacuous. G(0) is unused by the generated trace; output bounds concern new increments after union, not necessarily raw proposal cardinality.

reconstruction: D10: Given the fixed target, L, traces A and Q, natural k, and a certificate as expanded in G06, every real α below the adversary limit recall yields guessed limit recall at least α/(k+1). The result also returns strict trace novelty, lower membership precision one, and lower tail precision one. The certificate already supplies the last three properties; its additional quantitative content is a vanishing-overhead eventual prefix-ratio inequality.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D10: ∀ {target L A Q k}, (hcert : BatchedPodsCertificate target L A Q k) → ∀ {α : Real}, α ≤ lowerRecall target A.limit → α / (k + 1 : Real) ≤ lowerRecall target Q.limit ∧ Novel A Q ∧ lowerMembershipPrecision L Q = 1 ∧ lowerTailPrecision L Q = 1.
algorithm_scope: D10: The certificate is a Type-valued object carrying a real overhead sequence, its convergence, and the other fields. It is supplied for the already fixed traces, before α; there is no existential G, new Q, procedure, or proof that an arbitrary run has such a certificate.
limitations:
D10: No independent infinitude, f-bound, admissibility of A, or sign condition on α is assumed outside the certificate. k is natural, so k+1 is positive. The prefix inequality is eventual, not all-time; overhead has limit zero with no sign or rate condition. Both precision conjuncts and novelty must be retained.

reconstruction: D11: If B contains every target-carrier element absent from A, its lower density in the target order is at least one minus the upper density of A in that same order. The upper statistic is limsup and the lower statistic is liminf.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D11: ∀ target : OrderedLanguage, ∀ A B : Language, target.carrier ∖ A ⊆ B → 1 - upperRecall target A ≤ lowerRecall target B.
algorithm_scope: D11: A and B are whole sets; there is no exhaustion, generator, computable inclusion test, or constructed B. The condition is a semantic set inclusion.
limitations:
D11: No requirement A ⊆ target.carrier, B ⊆ target.carrier, A ⊆ L, or disjointness is imposed; off-target elements do not enter the position count. Empty B is permitted when the inclusion holds. The conclusion is an asymptotic bound, not an exact complement identity or an all-prefix inequality.

reconstruction:
D12: On the particular run determined by G and A, every raw proposal at step n+1 is disjoint from the current adversary cumulative stage and from all previous cumulative generated guesses. It therefore prohibits repetitions of already generated elements in the raw batch, not merely repetitions that disappear when cumulative stages are formed by union.

D13: A supplied strict certificate for E, target, L, A, and Q implies strict trace novelty, cumulative lower membership precision one, and the lower recall bound given by the maximum of one minus adversary upper recall and one third of adversary lower recall. G08 expands every certificate premise: sparse-exploration precision accounting, already-supplied novelty, target-complement coverage, and already-supplied one-third recall bound.

D14: For every exploration set, real γ, ordered target, validity set, and pair of traces, a supplied gamma certificate implies the at-every-n historical novelty fraction bound GammaNovel, lower target recall exactly one, and lower cumulative membership precision exactly one. The certificate does not mention target: it requires, in particular, Set.univ ⊆ Q.limit, so the same certificate supports recall one for every ordered target.
quantifiers_and_dependencies:
D12: GeneratorNovel : BatchGenerator → Exhaustion → Prop; GeneratorNovel G A := ∀ n : Nat, Disjoint (G (n+1) (fun i : Fin(n+2) => A.stage i.val) (generatedStages G A n)) (A.stage (n+1) ∪ generatedStages G A n).

D13: ∀ E : ExplorationSet, ∀ target : OrderedLanguage, ∀ L : Language, ∀ A Q : Exhaustion, StrictNoveltyCertificate E target L A Q → Novel A Q ∧ lowerMembershipPrecision L Q = 1 ∧ max (1 - upperRecall target A.limit) (lowerRecall target A.limit / 3) ≤ lowerRecall target Q.limit.

D14: ∀ E : ExplorationSet, ∀ γ : Real, ∀ target : OrderedLanguage, ∀ L : Language, ∀ A Q : Exhaustion, GammaNoveltyCertificate E γ L A Q → GammaNovel γ A Q ∧ lowerRecall target Q.limit = 1 ∧ lowerMembershipPrecision L Q = 1.
algorithm_scope:
D12: G05 supplies the exact history and state interface and recurrence. This predicate is for one G,A pair and quantifies n only; it does not require novelty on every possible adversary or every hypothetical history, and does not construct or certify any G.

D13: E and both traces are universal parameters; a certificate is an additional hypothesis. This type gives no learner, algorithm producing traces, certificate constructor for arbitrary traces, or oracle/computability claim.

D14: This is conditional on a certificate for existing traces. G09 spells out the sparse-growth and invalid-count bounds, E.GammaAdmissible γ, the every-stage count bound for nonhistorically-novel output, and universal-set coverage. No G, computable procedure, or existence of such a certificate is asserted.
limitations:
D12: The n = 0 check concerns the proposal at step one and history stages zero and one; G at index zero is never tested. Empty proposals satisfy disjointness and progress is not required. A previously guessed element proposed again would violate this predicate even if the new increment is empty; the separate Novel predicate only tests increments against the current adversary.

D13: The sparse subcertificate forces cumulative size to tend to infinity. No f-bound, adversary subset/infinite assumption, lower tail precision conclusion, or generation-rate claim appears. Novelty and the one-third lower bound are certificate premises. Upper recall is a limsup and the final recall a liminf; the max conjunct must not be reduced to either bound alone.

D14: There is no explicit γ < 1 or γ ≥ 0 hypothesis; whatever restrictions are necessary are inherited from the certificate. GammaNovel only tests stages with positive cumulative size, and uses historical novelty, not Q_n ∖ A_n. No strict Novel or lower-tail-precision conclusion, step-size bound, or rate is included.

reconstruction: D15: For every real γ strictly below one, some exploration-set object E has its count in positions 1 through m bounded by (1−γ)m for every natural m. Because E is an ExplorationSet, its carrier is infinite, excludes one, has no consecutive members, and its same prefix-count ratio tends to zero.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D15: ∀ {γ : Real}, γ < 1 → ∃ E : ExplorationSet, ∀ m : Nat, (explorationCount E.carrier m : Real) ≤ (1 - γ) * (m : Real).
algorithm_scope: D15: The existential E may depend on γ. Its identity is unspecified by the type; there is no explicit construction, representation of γ, decidable membership, or uniform computable map γ ↦ E. This does not construct a generator or a gamma-certified trace.
limitations:
D15: γ need not be nonnegative. The count bound is all-prefix, including m = 0, where the interval is empty. The constructor does not exclude zero from the carrier, and zero is not counted by explorationCount. No quantitative decay rate is given and no admissibility result at γ = 1 is asserted.

reconstruction: D16: For the specifically named copying generator and every target, L, f, α, and admissible infinite A with lower recall at least α, its generated Q retains the bound f and the recall lower bound α, and has both lower membership precision and lower tail precision equal to one. G05 shows directly that this generator returns the current adversary cumulative stage and hence its generated cumulative stages equal those of A.
quantifiers_and_dependencies: D16: ∀ target : OrderedLanguage, ∀ L : Language, ∀ f : Nat → Nat, ∀ α : Real, ∀ A : Exhaustion, Infinite(A.limit) → A.limit ⊆ L → BoundedBy f A → α ≤ lowerRecall target A.limit → let Q := generatedExhaustion parrotGenerator A; BoundedBy f Q ∧ α ≤ lowerRecall target Q.limit ∧ lowerMembershipPrecision L Q = 1 ∧ lowerTailPrecision L Q = 1.
algorithm_scope: D16: The witness is exactly parrotGenerator, not an existential choice. At index t it uses the history entry t and ignores previous guessed state; generated execution supplies adversary stages through t. It requires no membership test in L or target at runtime. All four conclusion components concern this fixed named generated trace.
limitations:
D16: There is no novelty conclusion; copied new elements already lie in the current adversary stage. Raw cumulative proposals may be large, while the new increments satisfy f. No sign restriction on α, no target-carrier subset assumption, and no rate appear. Infinitude is an explicit premise and must not be omitted.

D18: For the fixed exhaustion with stage zero empty and every positive stage {0}, against the empty validity set, lower tail precision is exactly one and cumulative lower membership precision is exactly zero. This is a closed conjunction about the specified object, not an existential over an unspecified counterexample.

D18: lowerTailPrecision ∅ oneShotInvalidExhaustion = 1 ∧ lowerMembershipPrecision ∅ oneShotInvalidExhaustion = 0.
algorithm_scope:
